executive_summary: Store 424 Skerries recorded weekly sales of 394,761.22 inc VAT (361,766.91 ex VAT) for the week ending 27 June 2026, representing a solid trading performance for the period.
Overall store margin closed at 17.59%, with total waste of 3,036.38 representing a waste percentage of 0.84% of ex-VAT sales.

Several fresh departments are reporting cost of sales figures that are negative, indicating stock movements, opening stock values, or purchase data anomalies that require urgent investigation before these figures can be relied upon for decision-making.

Provisions is the most significant data anomaly this week, reporting a margin of 195.48% on sales of 26,098.97 with a negative COS of -24,918.71, driven by a closing stock figure of 25,129.61 against an opening stock of only 210.90 - this closing stock position must be verified immediately.

Produce similarly shows a negative COS of -11,162.64 with no opening stock recorded, producing an inflated margin of 126.38% on sales of 42,313.26 - an opening stock figure must be located or restated.

Fish waste of 522.70 is the second highest individual waste line and represents a meaningful margin drag on a department with sales of only 5,599.62, equating to approximately 9.3% waste-to-sales ratio for that category.
Provisions waste of 1,000.74 is the single largest waste line across all departments and requires a structured review of ordering, ranging, and date code management.

The aggregate department TOTAL shows purchases recorded as zero, confirming that purchase data is absent across all fresh and counter departments this week - this must be resolved for accurate P&L reporting.
biggest_wins: Poultry delivered sales of 13,289.83 with a reported margin of 89.89%, and while stock movement distortions are present, the scan margin of 16.77% combined with strong sales volume indicates healthy underlying category performance.
Fish achieved sales of 5,599.62 with a scan margin of 17.79%, and despite high waste of 522.70, the counter is generating good top-line contribution relative to its footprint.

Deli posted sales of 10,663.41 with a scan margin of 39.38%, the highest scan margin of any department on the report, indicating strong theoretical profitability if waste and shrink are controlled - waste of 255.83 is manageable at current sales levels.

Produce generated the highest sales volume among fresh departments at 42,313.26, underpinning the store's fresh credentials, and waste of 888.48 should be assessed against this volume to determine whether the rate is acceptable.
Beef recorded sales of 13,832.32 with a scan margin of 19.48% and waste of only 64.49, indicating tight stock management and low shrink in a high-value protein category.
biggest_risks: Provisions closing stock of 25,129.61 against an opening stock of 210.90 with no purchases recorded is almost certainly a stock-take or data entry error - this single anomaly is distorting the entire department P&L and the total summary figures significantly.

Produce has no opening stock recorded, producing a negative COS of -11,162.64 and an artificial margin of 126.38% - an accurate opening stock figure must be sourced from the prior week's closing stock immediately.

Cigarettes is showing a negative COS of -3,572.55 with a reported margin of 146.68% against a scan margin of 12.96% - the closing stock of 131,469.13 exceeds opening stock of 127,896.58 with no purchases recorded, which is implausible and indicates a stock-take or system error.

Beef and Pork are also showing negative COS figures (Beef: -1,607.29, Pork: -61.26), again likely due to missing purchase data, meaning actual department profitability cannot be accurately assessed this week.

Provisions waste of 1,000.74 is the highest waste figure on the report and on a department with sales of 26,098.97 represents a material shrink concern that requires immediate review of ranging and rotation practices.
Fish waste of 522.70 on sales of 5,599.62 is disproportionately high - at approximately 9.3% of department sales this is well above acceptable thresholds and risks eroding any margin generated.

Dairy waste of 403.77 and bread and cakes waste of 390.75 are significant lines that do not have corresponding department P&L rows in this report, suggesting these categories are not being fully captured in the department-level analysis.
Frozen waste of 96.81, while not the largest line, should not be occurring at this level in a temperature-controlled category and warrants a review of freezer integrity and stock rotation.
department_callouts: Cigarettes: Reported margin of 146.68% versus scan of 12.96% is not credible - closing stock of 131,469.13 exceeds opening by 3,572.55 with zero purchases recorded; stock-take accuracy must be verified before this week's P&L is accepted.

Beef: Sales of 13,832.32 with a scan margin of 19.48% and waste of only 64.49 indicate strong counter discipline; negative COS of -1,607.29 is due to missing purchase data rather than a genuine stock gain.
Lamb: Sales of 1,490.55 with a scan margin of 24.11% and a positive COS of 324.77 make this the most reliably reported margin line in butchery; waste of 38.36 is well controlled.
Pork: Sales of 1,619.89 with a scan margin of 20.76%; negative COS of -61.26 suggests purchases are not captured; waste of 6.96 is the lowest of all fresh departments - excellent shrink control.

Bacon and Loose SRP: Sales of 876.64 with a scan margin of 11.26%, the lowest scan margin in the butchery cluster; COS of 290.13 produces a reported margin of 66.90% which is distorted by missing purchases - the low scan margin warrants a pricing and mix review.
Poultry: Sales of 13,289.83 with a scan margin of 16.77% and waste of 30.29; reported margin of 89.89% is distorted by stock movement anomalies but underlying category is performing well at volume.
Fish: Sales of 5,599.62 with a scan margin of 17.79%; waste of 522.70 is severely elevated relative to sales and requires an urgent ordering and date code review to protect margin.

Produce: Highest fresh sales at 42,313.26 with a scan margin of 19.06%; no opening stock recorded creates a meaningless reported margin of 126.38% - opening stock restatement is required and waste of 888.48 should be benchmarked against category sales.

Deli: Sales of 10,663.41 with the strongest scan margin on the floor at 39.38%; waste of 255.83 is broadly acceptable at this sales level; negative COS of -270.48 reflects stock build rather than genuine surplus and should be monitored.

Provisions: Sales of 26,098.97 with a scan margin of 19.48%; closing stock of 25,129.61 against opening of 210.90 with no purchases is a clear data error inflating margin to 195.48%; waste of 1,000.74 is the highest single waste line on the report and must be actioned regardless of the stock-take issue.
action_plan: Investigate and correct the Provisions stock-take immediately - closing stock of 25,129.61 against opening stock of 210.90 with no purchases recorded is not credible and is materially distorting store-level P&L figures.
Locate the missing Produce opening stock figure from the prior week closing stock report and restate the Produce department P&L before this week's figures are finalised or shared upward.

Confirm that purchase data has not been loaded for any counter department this week and escalate to the accounts or systems team to resolve the data feed so that accurate COGS can be calculated for Beef, Pork, Poultry, Fish, Deli, and all other affected departments.

Verify the Cigarettes closing stock count of 131,469.13 - a closing stock exceeding opening by over 3,500 with no purchases is implausible in a controlled tobacco category and likely reflects a count or system entry error.

Conduct an urgent review of Fish ordering and date code management - waste of 522.70 on sales of 5,599.62 is approximately 9.3% waste-to-sales and must be reduced through tighter daily ordering aligned to actual rate of sale.

Review Provisions ranging, order quantities, and markdown procedures to address waste of 1,000.74 - identify the specific lines driving this waste and consider reducing range width or implementing earlier markdown triggers.

Benchmark Produce waste of 888.48 against the department's actual sales rate and implement daily waste recording by sub-category to identify whether waste is concentrated in specific lines such as loose produce or pre-packed salads.

Conduct a Bacon and Loose SRP pricing and product mix review given the scan margin of 11.26% is the lowest in the butchery cluster - assess whether any lines are priced below cost or whether promotional activity is eroding margin.

Review dairy waste of 403.77 and bread and cakes waste of 390.75 at department level - these are significant waste lines not reflected in the department P&L table and require dedicated management attention and daily date code checks.
Investigate frozen waste of 96.81 - check freezer temperatures, door seal integrity, and stock rotation practices to eliminate avoidable shrink in a category where waste should be near zero.

Schedule a formal stock accuracy audit across Cigarettes, Provisions, and Produce before next week's stock-take to ensure opening figures are verified and reliable, preventing a repeat of this week's P&L distortions.

Prepare a corrected version of this week's department P&L incorporating restated stock figures and, once purchase data is recovered, recalculate accurate COGS and margin percentages for all departments before the week is closed on the system.
